_comment: ELECTRONICS StoreProfile (P5, electronics-first). This is the CONSOLIDATED home for everything laptop/electronics-SPECIFIC that is currently hardcoded across recommend.py (~115 flavour lines), use_case_advisor.py, query_decomposer.py, nqe.py, plus the existing store_vocab.json + verticals/electronics.json. It is BOTH the scaffold for the agnostic core AND the excision map: every slot below names a place in code that should READ from here instead of hardcoding. The agents (Candidate_Retrieval, Product_Ranking, Spec_Filter, Device_Match, Budget_Guard, NQE, Policy_Gate, ...) are agnostic MECHANISMS and do NOT move; only this FLAVOUR moves. Adding a second profile (pharmacy.json) with the same shape is the agnostic proof.
_nqe_brand_detect_comment: Laptop MAKERS only (for NQE brand-preference detection) — deliberately excludes component makers (intel/amd/nvidia) that appear in known_brands for claim-guard but must not be read as a buyer's brand choice. Matches the list excised from nqe.py.
_prohibited_claim_patterns_comment: Send-cage EXTENSION (fulfillment/draft.claim_safety_reason). These regexes ADD to the hardcoded governance floor (we-guarantee / order-confirmed / price-match / PO-confirmed) — they can only TIGHTEN the cage, never weaken it. Electronics-specific over-promises a procurement RFQ must never assert (counterfeit/grey-market/condition claims). A malformed pattern is skipped fail-safe; the floor always applies.
_manufacturers_comment: 3-AXIS brand identity (separates manufacturer / product line / from product TYPE which lives in product_type_rules). 'lines' are the sub-brands / product ranges (ThinkPad, XPS, ROG); 'aliases' are manufacturer-name tokens. brand_label_patterns (image->manufacturer) and the brand alias index are DERIVED from this single source (store_profile.brand_label_patterns / product_line_index) so the three scattered brand dicts in recommend.py collapse to one. A vertical fills the same three axes with its own flavour.
_use_case_budget_floors_comment: Minimum viable price (USD) per use-case — excised from recommend_budget_advisor._USE_CASE_BUDGET_FLOORS. Vertical-EXCLUSIVE (prefer-profile, not union): a pharmacy must not inherit gaming floors.
_safe_image_comment: Curated SAFE allow-list for fast-path image hinting (a bounded subset that may steer retrieval). Separate from manufacturers/primary_types so the security allow-list is explicit and auditable per vertical.
_category_keywords_comment: grounding-ladder category vocab (excised from grounding_ladder._CATEGORY_KW). token lists per category for query/identity grounding. A non-electronics vertical supplies its own.
_product_type_rules_comment: Ordered classification rules (FIRST match wins; accessory/specific types BEFORE 'laptop' so 'Laptop Brief' -> bag). Migrated VERBATIM from the archived store_vocab.json so product_classifier (the one taxonomy brain) reads flavour from the profile. spec_units/gpu_prefixes feed product_claim_guard.

product_type_rules.pattern: \b(ssd|hdd|hard drive|flash drive|usb drive|sd card|micro ?sd|memory card|portable ssd|external drive|nvme drive)\b
\b(mouse|keyboard|webcam|docking station|dock\b|usb hub|hub\b|laptop stand|stand\b|cooling pad|charger|power adapter|adapter|hdmi|ethernet cable|cable|card reader)\b

_use_case_fit_markers_comment: Soft/exclusion vocabulary for use_case_fit (B2B/fleet ranking). Markers are matched as lowercase substrings against the candidate's name + specs JSON. score_adjustment = (soft weight x matched soft signals) + (exclusion weight x matched exclusions). The vocabulary lives HERE (profile), so the core scorer only applies the returned number and stays vertical-agnostic.
_evidence_markers_comment: Marker groups for per-pick narration evidence (recommend_evidence). DATA only — opaque substrings matched against a candidate's name+specs+features for the portability/docking/warranty/os_ecosystem metrics. The fleet/office metrics reuse use_case_soft_markers.
_recommendation_lanes_comment: Backend choice-lanes (recommend_choice_lanes). DATA only — markers/exclusions are opaque substrings matched against a candidate's name+specs+features; the core just groups. A candidate joins the highest-priority lane whose marker matches and whose exclusions don't. `primary_for` lists the use-cases for which the lane is a PRIMARY pick; `non_primary` lanes (gaming chassis) are never primary, so a work query never surfaces gaming as a top office pick.

recommendation_lanes.title: Windows Business
recommendation_lanes.explain: Business-class Windows laptops: manageability (vPro/TPM), docking, warranty and fleet imaging.

recommendation_lanes.title: Apple / MacBook
recommendation_lanes.explain: MacBooks: battery life, build quality, the macOS ecosystem and MDM support.

recommendation_lanes.title: Microsoft Surface
recommendation_lanes.explain: Surface: portable 2-in-1 productivity with pen support and Windows Hello.

recommendation_lanes.title: Chromebook
recommendation_lanes.explain: Chromebooks: low cost, easy central management, web/cloud workloads.

recommendation_lanes.title: Budget / Consumer
recommendation_lanes.explain: Thin consumer laptops: lowest cost, but fewer business-management features.

recommendation_lanes.title: High-performance (discrete GPU)
recommendation_lanes.explain: Powerful discrete-GPU laptops — the right pick for GPU-heavy work (AI/ML model training, content/video editing, 3D/CAD) and gaming. For normal office work they are a poor fit (thermals, battery, weight, webcam/conferencing), so they are demoted there.
recommendation_lanes._primary_for_comment: PRIMARY for gaming AND GPU-heavy use-cases; `specialty` demotes it to non-primary only for queries NOT in this list (e.g. office/corporate).

_storefront_emphasis_comment: Phase-3 storefront-emphasis variants (David Module 4/5). DATA copy only — never free-form LLM. The experiment-gated, reversible lever picks one per TREATMENT subject; control gets none. Vertical-flavoured strings live HERE (profile), the core lever stays vertical-blind.

storefront_emphasis_variants.value: Great value picks — performance per dollar, matched to your budget.
storefront_emphasis_variants.urgency: Popular right now and moving fast — secure your pick before stock shifts.
storefront_emphasis_variants.features: Spec-forward picks — the capabilities that matter for your use-case, up front.

_nqe_question_packs_comment: Domain-specific NQE clarifying questions (excised from nqe.py hardcoded packs). Each entry is keyed by question id and contains: text, goal, evidence_needed, source, options. NQE reads these from the active profile; non-electronics verticals supply their own domain questions.

_use_case_patterns_comment: Detection regexes excised from query_decomposer._USE_CASE_PATTERNS (R2). Sources are byte-identical to the inline fallback (parity-tested). dgpu_use_cases derives from use_cases[*].needs_dedicated_gpu.

use_case_patterns.office: \b(office work|office laptop|office staff|for staff|our staff|company staff|staff laptops?|excel|spreadsheet|word processing|email|business|corporate|enterprise|professional|work laptops?|for work|productivity)\b

_hard_constraint_rules_comment: Spec-constraint extraction rules excised VERBATIM from query_decomposer._extract_hard_constraints (NEW-2) so that function is vertical-blind. Each rule: pattern (regex), key (constraint), cast (int|float), group (capture #), optional multiplier. Non-electronics verticals carry their own (or none) — no GPU/refresh/RAM bleed.
_hard_constraint_metric_map_comment: Adapter mapping from normalized query constraints to extracted product metrics. The core ranking engine only evaluates these declarative operators.
_ranking_conflict_rules_comment: Adapter-only workload/chassis conflicts. Strong deltas prevent generic stock and price bonuses from presenting a known mismatch as a best fit.

conditions.reason: gaming chassis conflicts with the requested business use
gaming-first chassis is a weaker fit for everyday study

_use_case_spec_implications_comment: Implied spec floors when a use-case is present AND a phrase matches (e.g. competitive/esports gaming implies a high refresh floor). mode=setdefault never overrides an explicit value.
_use_case_keyword_map_comment: Detailed use-case keyword matching map (excised from use_case_advisor.match_use_case_from_query). Each key is a use-case slug; value is a list of keywords. First-match scoring with priority tie-break. Vertical-exclusive: pharmacy must NOT inherit gaming/GPU use-cases.
_entity_comment: Entity-NER slots (category/brand/use-case/spec patterns + image-label map) excised VERBATIM from services/category_router.py so that module is vertical-blind. Non-electronics verticals derive these from their own manufacturers/use_case_patterns/product_type_rules via the accessor fallbacks.
_accessory_taxonomy_comment: Accessory FAMILY taxonomy (family codes / SKU-prefix map / keyword + slug maps / type->family) excised VERBATIM from services/product_taxonomy.py so that module is vertical-blind. Non-electronics verticals that define no taxonomy slots get UNK families (no electronics-accessory bleed); they can add their own family taxonomy later.
_persona_patterns_comment: ADAPTER: buyer-persona detection keywords (recommend_persona core algo is vertical-blind). Phase 2A P0.
_brand_sql_patterns_comment: ADAPTER (Phase 2A P0): brand -> SQL WHERE-fragment for catalog filtering. TRUSTED CONFIG ONLY (interpolated into SQL; no user input reaches these strings). Excised verbatim from recommend_candidate_classify.brand_sql_predicate. Non-electronics verticals derive predicates from their manufacturers slot.

brand_sql_patterns.hp: (LOWER(p.name) LIKE '%hp %' OR LOWER(p.name) LIKE 'hp %' OR LOWER(p.name) LIKE '%envy%' OR LOWER(p.name) LIKE '%victus%' OR LOWER(p.name) LIKE '%omen%' OR LOWER(p.name) LIKE '%omnibook%' OR LOWER(p.name) LIKE '%elitebook%' OR LOWER(p.name) LIKE '%probook%')
brand_sql_patterns.dell: (LOWER(p.name) LIKE '%dell%' OR LOWER(p.name) LIKE '%inspiron%' OR LOWER(p.name) LIKE '%xps%' OR LOWER(p.name) LIKE '%latitude%' OR LOWER(p.name) LIKE '%vostro%')

_persona_prompt_templates_comment: ADAPTER (Phase 2A P1): ordered first-match rules -> persona-calibrated LLM prompt block. Match if buyer_persona in personas OR use_case in use_cases OR any substring in use_cases_contains. Excised verbatim from recommend_persona.build_persona_prompt_context.

persona_prompt_templates.text:
Shopper: High school student (or a parent buying for them). Budget-conscious. Needs to survive a full school day.
Emphasize: Battery life (8+ hours for school), how light and easy it is to carry, screen quality for reading and note-taking. A 2-in-1 or stylus support is a bonus.
Tone: Simple and reassuring — no jargon. Say 'lasts all day on one charge' not '60Wh'. Say 'easy to carry to school' not '1.4kg'. Mention homework, notes, and streaming.
Avoid: Gaming GPU specs, benchmark numbers, enterprise language.

Shopper: University student. Balances lectures, research, socializing, and light media. Moderate budget.
Emphasize: Portability + build quality (campus life is rough), battery for lecture days, enough RAM (16 GB) for browser tabs + note-taking + the occasional assignment crunch. A good keyboard matters.
Tone: Relatable and encouraging — say 'handles 20 browser tabs and Zoom at the same time without breaking a sweat'. Mention real uni workflows (Google Docs, research PDFs, Netflix between classes).
Avoid: Heavy workstation specs. Keep it practical and fun.

Shopper: Engineering / CS / architecture student. Runs simulation, CAD, or ML workloads that push hardware.
Emphasize: RAM (32 GB strongly preferred — MATLAB, Docker, multiple VMs), dedicated GPU (even mid-range helps with CUDA / rendering), fast storage (SSD for large projects), build quality.
Tone: Technically literate but outcome-focused — say 'compiles large projects 3× faster' not 'Intel i7-13700H at 4.9 GHz'. Reference real tools: MATLAB, SolidWorks, Docker, VS Code with containers.
Avoid: Generic 'fast processor' language. These students know what CUDA cores do.

Shopper: Data scientist / AI-ML engineer. Trains models, runs Jupyter notebooks, maybe fine-tunes LLMs locally.
Emphasize: GPU VRAM (12 GB+ for training), RAM (32-64 GB for large datasets), fast NVMe (dataset I/O), CUDA support (NVIDIA). A big display helps with notebooks.
Tone: Peer-level technical — say '12 GB VRAM lets you fine-tune 7B-param models locally', 'enough RAM to keep your entire dataset in memory'. Reference PyTorch, HuggingFace, Jupyter.
Avoid: Basic office specs. This shopper needs GPU horsepower.

Shopper: Content creator / video editor. Works in Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or After Effects. Color-accuracy matters.
Emphasize: Color-accurate display (100% sRGB / DCI-P3), GPU for timeline preview (dedicated GPU strongly preferred), 32+ GB RAM (timeline scrubbing with effects), fast storage (proxy + export).
Tone: Creative-pro — say 'scrubs 4K timelines without dropping frames', 'colors you can trust for client work'. Mention real workflows: color grading, multicam, After Effects compositions.
Avoid: Gaming-focused language (refresh rate, FPS). These shoppers care about color, not frames.

Shopper: Gamer. Performance per dollar is king. Wants smooth frame rates in the titles they play.
Emphasize: GPU tier (name the chip and what it means for their games — e.g. '4060 handles 1080p high settings at 80+ FPS in most titles'), high-refresh display (120+ Hz), thermal design (sustained performance, not throttling). RAM 16 GB is the sweet spot.
Tone: Enthusiast but practical — say 'runs Cyberpunk at 60 FPS on High' not just 'RTX 4070'. Translate specs into FPS/resolution outcomes. Mention specific popular games if the query names them.
Avoid: Battery life focus (gamers usually plug in). Avoid enterprise/office language.

Shopper: Business professional / corporate user. Productivity, reliability, and security trump raw performance.
Emphasize: Reliability and build quality (ThinkPad-tier), manageability (TPM, vPro if relevant), battery for meeting-to-meeting days, keyboard comfort, display clarity for spreadsheets and presentations.
Tone: Professional and outcome-focused — say 'reliable enough you'll never miss a deadline', 'crisp display for hours of spreadsheet work'. Mention Teams, Outlook, multi-monitor setups.
Avoid: Gaming specs, RGB lighting references. This is a tool purchase, not a toy.

Shopper: Finance / accounting professional. Lives in Excel, ERP systems, and multi-monitor setups.
Emphasize: Keyboard comfort (numbers entry for hours), display clarity (dense spreadsheets), multi-monitor support (Thunderbolt/USB-C docking), 32 GB RAM (large workbooks with pivot tables + Power Query).
Tone: Efficiency-focused — say 'handles your largest workbooks without lag', 'connects to dual monitors with a single cable'. Mention Excel, Power BI, ERP systems.
Avoid: GPU/gaming language. A discrete GPU is wasted spend here.

Shopper: Medical student. Long study sessions, anatomy software, and clinical placement demands.
Emphasize: Battery life (clinical placements without outlets), portability (ward rounds), display quality (anatomy diagrams and imaging), reliability.
Tone: Supportive and practical — say 'lasts through a full day on the ward', 'clear enough for detailed anatomy diagrams'. Mention Anki, anatomy apps, clinical databases.
Avoid: Gaming specs. A discrete GPU is unnecessary for med school.

Shopper: Law student. Case briefs, legal research databases, long reading/writing sessions. Pure productivity.
Emphasize: Battery life (long library sessions), keyboard comfort (typing-heavy work — briefs, essays, memos), display clarity (reading-heavy), reliability.
Tone: No-nonsense and direct. Say 'handles long case brief sessions without slowing down', 'comfortable to type on for hours'. Pure productivity focus.
Avoid: GPU/gaming specs. A discrete GPU is wasted spend for a law student.

Shopper: Frequent traveler. Works from airports, hotels, and client sites. Every gram and every hour of battery counts.
Emphasize: Weight (lighter is always better), battery life (8+ hours real-world), build quality (bumps happen in transit), USB-C charging (one less adapter to carry).
Tone: Practical and liberating. Say 'light enough to forget you're carrying it', 'lasts through a long-haul flight', 'tough enough for carry-on life'. Mention USB-C charging if available.
Avoid: Heavy workstation specs. Freedom from outlets and weight are the wins.

Shopper: Job hunter or career changer. Starting a new chapter — needs something professional-looking, reliable, and interview-ready.
Emphasize: Professional build and appearance (makes an impression), reliability, webcam and microphone quality (video interviews), keyboard comfort.
Tone: Encouraging and practical. Say 'professional build for interviews and the first day on the job', 'reliable enough that it never lets you down in a crucial moment'.
Avoid: Gaming specs. Focus on professionalism, reliability, and first impressions.

_identity_comment: ADAPTER (product identity / image+text): brand/product-type/form-factor/cpu keyword maps + spec regexes for identify_product_from_text. Excised VERBATIM from product_identity_agent. Verticals without these slots do not parse images through laptop identity fields (no bleed).
_product_identity_prompt_comment: ADAPTER: vision-LLM prompt/schema for identify_product_from_image. Electronics laptop schema; a vertical without this slot gets a generic identify prompt (no laptop-schema bleed).
product_identity_prompt:
You are a product identification specialist for an ecommerce platform.
Analyze this product image and extract structured specifications.
Return ONLY valid JSON (no markdown, no prose).
Schema:
{
  "identified": true|false,
  "product_type": "laptop|desktop|tablet|phone|monitor|accessory|other",
  "brand": "string or null",
  "model": "string or null",
  "cpu_tier": "budget|midrange|performance|workstation|unknown",
  "cpu_hint": "e.g. i5-13th, Ryzen 7, M2 Pro, or null",
  "ram_gb_hint": 8|16|32|null,
  "gpu_hint": "e.g. RTX 4060, integrated, or null",
  "display_inches_hint": 14|15.6|16|null,
  "form_factor": "ultrabook|standard|gaming|workstation|2-in-1|unknown",
  "price_tier": "budget|midrange|premium|flagship|unknown",
  "confidence": 0.0 to 1.0,
  "notes": "short free-text"
}
Rules:
- Identify from visible branding, form factor, bezels, keyboard layout, chassis design.
- If you see visible text (model label, spec sticker), use it.
- If uncertain about a field, use null or unknown.
- confidence reflects overall identification certainty.
